summary.intent: Plan and execute phase 49 (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation ECIES unwrap consolidation), then run PR-QA (simplify, security-review, CodeRabbit CLI) before pushing and opening a PR.
summary.outcome: Planning completed (5 plans, 3 waves, 6 requirements, plan-check passed after one revision round). Execution started: Wave 1 plan 49-01 (SDK layer, TDD) completed; 49-02 dispatched but transcript ends before confirmation.

repo: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange is fully key-agnostic (takes raw key bytes) — reusable verbatim for the shared-folder move case without modification.
share_keys entries are keyed by itemId (file UUID), not parent folder — file keys do NOT need re-registration after a folder move.
adoptSharedFolderResult must be called only once for the source result; calling it for the dest would corrupt the sharedFolderTree projection (dual-emit problem).
File IPNS key for re-encryption must come from share_keys keyType:'file-ipns', NOT FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted (owner-wrapped, recipient cannot decrypt it).
sdkCore.moveItem collision policy: throws 'An item with this name already exists in destination' — no auto-rename logic needed.
SharedFolderClient Pick allowlist in shared-folder-projection.ts:28-38 must be extended to include moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree.

Batch move is a pure web-layer loop pattern (useFileBrowserActions → handleBatchMoveConfirm → useFolderMutations.handleMoveItems) — no dedicated SDK batch method; single-item moveInSharedFolder is the correct atom.
useSharedWriteOps.test.ts already exists and is the correct place to add moveItemHandler unit tests.
Intel API surface regex extractor is unpopulated — the intel regeneration step produces an empty file and is HINT-only; RESEARCH.md carries all verified symbol refs.

code.finding: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange signature is key-agnostic (sourceFolderKey/destFolderKey/fileIpnsPrivateKey as raw bytes) — directly reusable for the shared case.
Pick allowlist for SharedFolderClient only listed the 7 Phase 48 methods; moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree must be added.
moveItem throws on name collision with 'An item with this name already exists in destination' — propagates through runWrite → p.setError; no auto-rename path.

workflow: Sequential plan execution (no parallel worktrees) is more reliable for autonomous/AFK runs — avoids cwd-drift and merge-base footguns in the worktree merge-back protocol.
Scope expansions (batch+drag added to REQ-6) should be folded in before the planner subagent is spawned — much cheaper than replanning.

CodeRabbit has two distinct review steps: CLI review (coderabbit review --agent) before PR creation, and an automatic GitHub review posted after PR creation that requires /resolve-pr-reviews to address.

Disabling local commit signing (git config --local commit.gpgsign false) is the correct approach for AFK automated GSD runs when 1Password signer would wedge; requires a signed rebase before merge due to branch protection.
Plan-checker is effective at catching real gaps: it identified missing REQ-3 unit test coverage (vacuously passing verify) that research doc nit fixups alone would not have caught.
gsd-tools is not on the PATH inside planner/revision subagents — planning artifacts that need commits must be committed by the orchestrator after the subagent returns.

friction: Commit signing (GPG via 1Password) wedges during AFK automated runs — required explicit local override (git config --local commit.gpgsign false) before execution could proceed autonomously.
Plan-checker blocker: REQ-3 (web single-item move) had no dedicated unit test, causing the verify gate to pass vacuously — required a targeted planner revision round.
Two plan-checker blockers were RESEARCH.md doc-formatting nits (missing resolution markers, wrong section heading), adding an unnecessary revision loop.
gsd-tools not on PATH inside revision subagent — subagent could not commit its own output, pushing the commit responsibility back to the orchestrator.
Intel API surface regeneration step produced an empty file (regex extractor unpopulated) — step is a no-op in this repo but still ran.
Parallel worktree execution had to be downgraded to sequential due to complexity of autonomous merge-back protocol — slower wall-clock.
